claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder prepared for L-PBF.
In situ substrate preheating is the proposed intervention during L-PBF.
Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients in the molten pool and surrounding material.
Reduced thermal gradients produce more uniform nucleation.
Substrate preheating leads to a finer grain structure.
Substrate preheating lowers the temperature differential during L-PBF.
Lowering the temperature differential slows the cooling rate.
Substrate preheating limits abrupt thermal shocks.
Reduced undercooling minimizes the time available for solute diffusion.
Reduced undercooling and curtailed solute diffusion limit compositional segregation.
Substrate preheating decreases residual tensile stress.
Reduced segregation and residual stress decrease defect formation.
Preheated specimens will have lower residual stress than specimens produced by L-PBF without substrate preheating.
Preheated specimens will have less compositional segregation and a lower defect density than specimens produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated specimens will exhibit enhanced tensile strength.
Preheated specimens will exhibit enhanced ductility.
AlCrFeNiSi parts produced by L-PBF without substrate preheating typically have significant segregation and high residual stress.
Non-preheated L-PBF builds have defect-associated mechanical limitations.
The effects of substrate preheating depend on preheat temperature and other processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that preheating slows cooling but also that it minimizes the time available for solute diffusion. Those statements are internally inconsistent because slower cooling ordinarily implies a longer, not shorter, interval for diffusion.

The finer-grain mediator is mechanistically in tension with the claimed slower cooling and reduced undercooling; the hypothesis does not explain how those conditions would refine rather than coarsen the solidification structure.
